input.title: auto-merge delivery never lands on a repo with no PR CI — arm is rejected, PR sits open forever
input.body:
## The defect

GitHub's auto-merge is a **queue for checks**. On a repo with no `pull_request`-triggered workflow there is nothing to queue behind, so `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` is rejected outright ("Pull request is in clean status"). `deliver()` swallowed that:

```js
if (delivery === 'auto-merge' && pr?.node_id) {
  await enableAutoMerge(token, pr.node_id).catch(() => {});   // swallowed
}
```

So a member declaring `maintenance.delivery: auto-merge` gets **no merge at all**: the PR sits open, the stamp never advances, and the next cycle reuses the same PR and re-fails the same arm. Silently, forever.

## Scope

Seven of twelve consumers have no `pull_request` trigger anywhere in `.github/workflows` — LaughCounter, HelloWorldFlutterApp, EdFringeAllocator, Sheepdog, ShoutsAndWhispers, gRatio, VascularColoring. All declare `auto-merge`. That is most of the fleet.

The worker already *knew*: `dispatchCiRuns` logs "no pull_request-triggered workflow — the maintenance PR has no checks to wait for", and then did nothing with the fact.

This is distinct from #585 (the PR-open POST status was never read). #585 stopped the PR from being created at all; this one stops a created PR from ever landing. Fixing #585 alone would have left these seven repos stalled tonight, just one step later in the pipeline.

## Fix

`deliveryAction({ delivery, hasPrCi })` — a pure decision:

- `auto-merge` + no PR CI → **merge directly** (squash). No CI to wait for is what `auto-merge` meant all along.
- `auto-merge` + PR CI → arm, and let the checks gate it as designed.
- `review` → neither, unchanged.

`hasPrCi` comes from `ciDispatchPlan` over the branch's own workflow files (`dispatch` + `missing` both empty ⇒ nothing runs on a pull_request). That is a fact about the tree, not a race against checks registering. A dispatch failure leaves `hasPrCi` **true** — unknown never merges blind.

The arm's failure is now logged with the repo setting to check, rather than swallowed.

## Known remaining gap

A repo whose PR CI exists but is **path-filtered away** from `.claudinite/**` (TLDR: all three workflows filter to `extension/**`, `server/**`, `dev/requirements/**`) counts as `hasPrCi: true`, so its maintenance PR arms and waits for checks that will never run. Evaluating path filters against the diff is a bigger change; deliberately not attempted here. TLDR's `maintenance.delivery` can be set to `review` in the meantime, or a `workflow_dispatch`-able conformance workflow added.

---

input.title: Adoption never sets the two repo settings baselining depends on — add them to bootstrap (both are scriptable)
input.body:
Baselining's delivery depends on two repository settings that **nothing in adoption ever sets, checks, or mentions**. `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/adopt-claudinite/SKILL.md` has zero references to either — the only mentions anywhere in the corpus are the error strings added by #585.

Both are the direct cause of the two-day fleet stall.

## The settings

| Setting | UI | API |
|---|---|---|
| Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests | Settings → Actions → General | `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/permissions/workflow` → `{"can_approve_pull_request_reviews": true}` |
| Allow auto-merge | Settings → General → Pull Requests | `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}` → `{"allow_auto_merge": true}` |

**Both are readable and writable by script** — plain REST, no UI-only step. The matching `GET` on each returns the current value, so a conformance check could assert them rather than only bootstrap setting them.

The constraint is the credential, not the API: both require **admin** on the repo. The Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot do it, so this cannot be self-healed by baselining from inside the member. It belongs to either:

- **adoption** (`adopt-claudinite`), which already runs in a session with the owner's own credentials, or
- **the sheepdog pack**, whose `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` spans the account — it could converge both settings fleet-wide alongside `fleet-freshness`, and would catch a repo whose settings were later flipped back.

The second is the stronger option: adoption sets it once, whereas the sheepdog sweep keeps it true.

## Why it matters

Without the first, the maintenance PR is never created (#585 — silent before that fix, loud after). Without the second, an `auto-merge` member's PR opens and never lands. Neither is visible from inside the member repo, and neither produced any signal until it was investigated by hand.

## Suggested scope

1. Adoption sets both over the owner's credentials, and records what it set.
2. A check (or the sheepdog freshness sweep) asserts both remain true, reporting the exact API path when they are not.
3. `adopt-claudinite` documents them, so a hand-adopted repo does not silently miss them.

# sheepdog

The fleet **enforcer** marker — declaring it makes a repo the one that covers and maintains every repo
under an owner. Opt-in (a dedicated sheepdog repo declares it; **not** seeded by `--init`). It
standardizes the fleet coverage that used to be bespoke Claudinite infrastructure into a declaration.

Thin by design: prose + the config schema (the sheepdog pack entry's `config` = `{ owner, kind, exclude,
canonRepo, staleDays }`) + three cross-repo **sweeps**, each with the one agentless scheduled task that
runs it (the sweep is its `agent_preprocessing`; no workflow of its own):

| sweep | task | asks |
|---|---|---|
| [check-fleet-coverage.mjs](tasks/fleet-census/check-fleet-coverage.mjs) | [fleet-census](tasks/fleet-census/task.md) (daily) | is this repo a **member**? → adoption issues |
| [check-fleet-freshness.mjs](tasks/fleet-freshness/check-fleet-freshness.mjs) | [fleet-freshness](tasks/fleet-freshness/task.md) (weekly) | is a member **keeping up**? → drift issues |
| [aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs](tasks/fleet-usage/aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs) | [fleet-usage](tasks/fleet-usage/task.md) (daily) | what does the fleet **actually use**? → `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` |

The second exists because per-project scheduling made every member maintain itself and, in doing so,
removed the last thing that looked at a member from the **outside** — self-maintenance cannot detect its
own absence. The third exists for the same shape of reason one rung up: a member can say whether a
skill loads *there*, and only a view across every member can say whether it earns its place at all.

A member that declares itself **dormant** (`"dormant": true` in its own declaration) is out of the
freshness sweep and out of the usage denominator — its scheduler is stopped, so its mount falls
behind by design and its silence says nothing about any skill. It stays a **member**: the census
is unchanged, because dormancy is about upkeep, not membership.

Each sweep lives **inside its task's folder**, because nothing outside that task uses it. Only what
both share sits at the pack root: [fleet-api.mjs](fleet-api.mjs) (the cross-repo REST primitives) and
[fleet-config.mjs](fleet-config.mjs) (the one reader of this pack's entry `config`).

The rest of the machinery — running the daily-run, the task engine (`engine/scheduler/`), scheduling —
is Claudinite **core**. Carries no conformance checks. Policy + config: [RULES.md](RULES.md).

# sheepdog — the fleet enforcer marker

Declaring this pack marks a repo as the **fleet enforcer**: the one repo that covers and maintains
every repo under an owner. It's opt-in — a dedicated `sheepdog` repo declares it (it is **not** seeded
by `--init`).

It contributes the pieces only a fleet enforcer needs — three **cross-repo sweeps** — plus their config
schema and the scheduled tasks that run them. The rest of the machinery — running the daily-run (the
orchestrator), the task engine (`engine/scheduler/`), scheduling — is Claudinite **core**, because
baselining and the daily-run are Claudinite's own responsibility, not the pack's.

**Three sweeps, three questions** — separate, because they close on unrelated conditions. The
**census** ([check-fleet-coverage.mjs](tasks/fleet-census/check-fleet-coverage.mjs)) asks *is this repo a
member* and converges `fleet-adoption` issues. The **freshness sweep**
([check-fleet-freshness.mjs](tasks/fleet-freshness/check-fleet-freshness.mjs)) takes coverage as given, asks *is that
membership still meaning anything*, and converges `fleet-drift` issues. The second exists because
per-project scheduling made every member maintain itself and removed the last outside look at one:
self-maintenance cannot detect its own absence. The **usage sweep**
([aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs](tasks/fleet-usage/aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs)) asks *what does the fleet
actually use* and writes `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` — a file, not issues, because it reports a
measurement rather than a condition to converge. It exists because a member folds its own skill-usage
numbers and can therefore only say whether a skill loads *there*; whether a skill earns its place at
all is fleet-shaped, and nothing inside a member can see it.

**Where the code lives** — each sweep sits **inside its task's folder**, because only that task's
`worker.mjs` uses it. The pack root holds just what both need: [fleet-api.mjs](fleet-api.mjs) (cross-repo
REST primitives) and [fleet-config.mjs](fleet-config.mjs) (the one reader of the entry `config` below).

**Config** — this repo's `.claudinite-checks.json` carries, as its `packs` entry for this pack:

```json
{ "id": "sheepdog", "config": { "owner": "missingbulb", "kind": "user", "exclude": ["owner/repo-a"],
                                "canonRepo": "missingbulb/Claudinite", "staleDays": 14 } }
```

`owner` (default: this repo's owner) is who to cover; `exclude` is the repos deliberately kept out of
the fleet (a full `owner/name` each) — a repo is kept out by adding it here. `kind: "user"` today; org
support is a later addition. `canonRepo` (default `<owner>/Claudinite`) is what a member's stamped ref
is measured against — named rather than inferred, because a ref tells you nothing about where it came
from. `staleDays` (default `14`) is how far behind is too far. Both are freshness-only and both
default, so an existing sheepdog config keeps working untouched.

[`fleet-freshness`](tasks/fleet-freshness/task.md) (`weekly`) and
[`fleet-usage`](tasks/fleet-usage/task.md) (`daily`) scheduled tasks, all `agent_model: none`, each

A short note in `packs/sheepdog/RULES.md`, next to "When they fail".

input.title: Nothing proves a canon change is safe for consumers — add a baselining rehearsal, a startup self-test, and a rule for core/pack changes
input.body:
## The gap, in one line

**Canon CI proves the canon is healthy. Nothing proves what a canon change does to a consumer on its next baselining.**

Green canon CI is not evidence about consumers, because the canon's own packs are always already migrated. Every consumer-breaking change today passed canon CI cleanly.

## Evidence from a single day

| change | canon CI | effect on consumers |
|---|---|---|
| #555 — pack manifest becomes a closed vocabulary, `ruleRoutingGuidance` required, no migration record | ✅ green | **11 local packs across 10 repos blocked**; because `normalizeManifest` rebuilds `rules` from the scoped lists, each pack's checks **silently stopped running** |
| #585 — PR-open POST status never read | ✅ green | maintenance PR never created; 27 orphan branches; 12 repos frozen 2 days, run reporting `ok` |
| #588 — auto-merge armed on repos with no PR CI | ✅ green | 7 repos would open a PR that never lands |
| (this session) converge run from an unmerged canon branch | n/a | every member stamped off-trunk — the #328 anti-rewind guard would have **wedged all 13** on the next run |

Three of the four are *invisible until a consumer runs*, and the fourth was invisible until someone read the stamps by hand.

## Proposal — three layers, smallest first

### 1. A startup self-test (the owner's idea, and the highest value per unit of work)

A fast, **mechanism-only** verification — "can Claudinite run here?" — explicitly *not* "does this repo pass its rules". Distinct from `check_the_world`, which judges repo content.

Asserts, in well under a second:

- the mount exists and `.claudinite-checks.json` parses, with a readable stamp
- **every declared pack resolves and its manifest validates** ← would have caught #555 at session start on every consumer, the same day
- declared local packs exist at their declared paths
- hooks in `.claude/settings.json` point at files that exist ← the class of #397 (`inject-pack-prose` importing a nonexistent module, silently un-injected fleet-wide)
- the scheduler workflow is present and its cron parses
- mounted skills resolve (no dangling links) ← the class of #424
- the migrations registry loads

**Where it runs:** the SessionStart hook (report-only, never blocking a session), at the end of bootstrap, and at the end of baselining preprocessing — where a failure is exactly the signal that should request the agent instead of reporting `ok`.

### 2. A baselining rehearsal in canon CI

The direct answer to *"how do we check baselining would work, with and without a migration?"*

Fixture consumers in the canon (one per shape: local packs + rules, prose-only local pack, no local pack, chrome-extension, flutter). For each, CI runs the **real** converge — `apply-vendor-set` → `converge-wiring` → `migrations/apply` — then the startup self-test and `check_the_world`.

Run in **two modes**, which is what makes it answer the migration half:

- **fresh**: fixture stamped at canon HEAD~ → the ordinary nightly path
- **stale**: fixture pinned at an old stamp → forces migration *selection* to fire, so a record that is missing, misdated, or not idempotent shows up as a red canon PR

A canon PR that would turn a consumer red fails **before it merges**. That is the gate that did not exist for #555.

### 3. A rule for changes to core and to packs

Encoded as a check over the diff, not just prose. A change that:

- adds or makes required a **manifest field**, or
- changes a **check's severity** or a rule's id, or
- alters a **vendored contract** (engine module signature, task field, stub shape)

must ship **either** a migration record **or** a rehearsal fixture demonstrating consumers stay green — and must say which in the PR. Today's `consumer-safe-changes.md` states the principle; nothing enforces it.

## Note on #555 specifically

A migration record for #555 is **not** worth adding now, and could not have fixed it anyway: a record's ops are aliases / materialize / rewrite — literal replacements. `rules` → `worldRules` needs a per-rule scope judgment, and `ruleRoutingGuidance` is bespoke prose per pack. That is an **agentic** note at minimum. All 13 members are now migrated and stamped after it, so a record today would be a no-op that then needs retiring. The durable protection is layers 2 and 3, not a retrospective record.

content.text: {"id":"5024358286","url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/592"}

Comment class: process-change (a defect fix, plus a design proposal)

**1 & 2 done** — [#591](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/591) adds the note to `packs/sheepdog/RULES.md`: converging those two settings alongside the freshness sweep is the natural home, but `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` isn't an admin token and both endpoints require admin — so the sweeps report the *symptom* (a member stuck `behind`), never the cause. Still open for your LGTM.

**4 — #555 and a migration record: my recommendation is no.** A record's ops are aliases/materialize/rewrite — literal replacements. `rules` → `worldRules` needed a per-rule scope judgment, and `ruleRoutingGuidance` is bespoke prose per pack; that's an *agentic* note at minimum, not a mechanical one. And all 13 members are now migrated and stamped after it, so a record today is a no-op that then needs retiring. The durable fix is the gate, not a retrospective record.

**Also:** `Empty` is not a Claudinite member (no `.claudinite-checks.json`) — so "all repos" really is 13, and I'd previously only checked 13 of 15.

## I broke something and caught it

The first re-baseline ran from my canon checkout while it sat on the **unmerged #591 branch**, so all 13 repos got stamped `47a0e729` — a commit that, after a squash merge, will *never* be an ancestor of `main`. That's precisely the `ref-not-on-trunk` shape: vendoring's #328 anti-rewind guard would have refused to write, **wedging every repo permanently**. Re-vendored from a rootless snapshot of `main`, stamped `f0b6377`, and verified all 13 are ancestors of main. Net: 26 PRs opened and merged, fleet correct.

## Your question is the right one — [#592](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/592)

The gap in one line: **canon CI proves the canon is healthy; nothing proves what a canon change does to a consumer.** Green canon CI is not evidence, because the canon's own packs are always already migrated. All four of today's breakages passed it cleanly.

The proposal, smallest-value-first:

1. **Your startup self-test** — mechanism-only ("can Claudinite run here?"), not rule evaluation. Manifests validate, hooks point at real files, skills resolve, scheduler cron parses, migrations registry loads. Runs at SessionStart, after bootstrap, and after baselining preprocessing. **It would have caught #555 on day one, on every consumer** — and the #397 class (hooks importing a nonexistent module) too.
2. **A baselining rehearsal in canon CI** — fixture consumers, the real converge, run in two modes: *fresh* (nightly path) and *stale* (pinned at an old stamp, so migration selection actually fires). That's the "with and without a migration" check you asked for, and it's the gate #555 needed.
3. **A rule for core/pack changes** — a required-field, severity, or vendored-contract change must ship either a migration record or a rehearsal fixture, enforced over the diff. `consumer-safe-changes.md` states the principle today; nothing enforces it.

> ⚠️ **Open:** #591 (sheepdog note) · #592 (the three-layer proposal — worth your call on scope before I build it) · #590 (settings in bootstrap) · TLDR still needs `delivery: review` or a dispatchable conformance workflow (#588) · 40 orphan branches now, UI-only deletion.
>
> **Tonight:** every repo carries the fixed worker and an on-trunk stamp, so baselining should open *and land* on all 13 — except TLDR, which will arm and wait on path-filtered CI that never runs.

# sheepdog — the fleet enforcer marker

Declaring this pack marks a repo as the **fleet enforcer**: the one repo that covers and maintains
every repo under an owner. It's opt-in — a dedicated `sheepdog` repo declares it (it is **not** seeded
by `--init`).

It contributes the pieces only a fleet enforcer needs — three **cross-repo sweeps** — plus their config
schema and the scheduled tasks that run them. The rest of the machinery — running the daily-run (the
orchestrator), the task engine (`engine/scheduler/`), scheduling — is Claudinite **core**, because
baselining and the daily-run are Claudinite's own responsibility, not the pack's.

**Three sweeps, three questions** — separate, because they close on unrelated conditions. The
**census** ([check-fleet-coverage.mjs](tasks/fleet-census/check-fleet-coverage.mjs)) asks *is this repo a
member* and converges `fleet-adoption` issues. The **freshness sweep**
([check-fleet-freshness.mjs](tasks/fleet-freshness/check-fleet-freshness.mjs)) takes coverage as given, asks *is that
membership still meaning anything*, and converges `fleet-drift` issues. The second exists because
per-project scheduling made every member maintain itself and removed the last outside look at one:
self-maintenance cannot detect its own absence. The **usage sweep**
([aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs](tasks/fleet-usage/aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs)) asks *what does the fleet
actually use* and writes `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` — a file, not issues, because it reports a
measurement rather than a condition to converge. It exists because a member folds its own skill-usage
numbers and can therefore only say whether a skill loads *there*; whether a skill earns its place at
all is fleet-shaped, and nothing inside a member can see it.

**Where the code lives** — each sweep sits **inside its task's folder**, because only that task's
`worker.mjs` uses it. The pack root holds just what both need: [fleet-api.mjs](fleet-api.mjs) (cross-repo
REST primitives) and [fleet-config.mjs](fleet-config.mjs) (the one reader of the entry `config` below).

**Config** — this repo's `.claudinite-checks.json` carries, as its `packs` entry for this pack:

```json
{ "id": "sheepdog", "config": { "owner": "missingbulb", "kind": "user", "exclude": ["owner/repo-a"],
                                "canonRepo": "missingbulb/Claudinite", "staleDays": 14 } }
```

`owner` (default: this repo's owner) is who to cover; `exclude` is the repos deliberately kept out of
the fleet (a full `owner/name` each) — a repo is kept out by adding it here. `kind: "user"` today; org
support is a later addition. `canonRepo` (default `<owner>/Claudinite`) is what a member's stamped ref
is measured against — named rather than inferred, because a ref tells you nothing about where it came
from. `staleDays` (default `14`) is how far behind is too far. Both are freshness-only and both
default, so an existing sheepdog config keeps working untouched.

**Classification** — all three sweeps are ordinary **pack tasks**, not fleet mechanisms. Their
*implementation* — an account-spanning PAT — happens to scan every repo under the owner, but their
declaration, scheduling, and lifecycle are exactly those of any pack task. None declares the
`fleet` signal nor `session_scope: fleet`; the cross-repo reach lives in the implementation, never in
how a task is wired. (The task files carry the same note.)

**How they run** — as the pack's [`fleet-census`](tasks/fleet-census/task.md) (`daily`),
[`fleet-freshness`](tasks/fleet-freshness/task.md) (`weekly`) and
[`fleet-usage`](tasks/fleet-usage/task.md) (`daily`) scheduled tasks, all `agent_model: none`, each
with its sweep as `agent_preprocessing`. The first two are `expected_outcome: none` (they open
**issues**, never a PR); the usage sweep is `merged-pr`, because its output IS a tracked file and an
auto-merging PR keeps that write inside the outcome taxonomy, lets this repo's CI gate a malformed
file, and makes the daily PR stream a browsable audit trail. Freshness is weekly because drift is
measured in days — a daily sweep would re-ask a question whose answer cannot have changed; usage is
daily because the members fold daily. There is **no coverage workflow** — preprocessing
runs Action-side inside this repo's one scheduler workflow, so the repo Actions secret is already
reachable there; each task's `required_secrets: ['FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN']` stamps the name into that
workflow's env and is what asks the owner for it (a fine-grained PAT spanning the owner's repos:
Metadata + Contents read, Issues read/write, and Contents write on this repo for baseline-migration
retirement — freshness adds no scope). A workflow that exists only to hold a secret is redundant
([packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md](../basics/scheduled-tasks.md)).

**What freshness assumes** — baselining reverts a stamp-only bump, so `claudinite.updated` advances
only when canon changed that member's vendor set. Age of the **stamped ref** is therefore the honest
liveness measure, and `behind` reads *"has not picked canon up in `staleDays`"*, not *"canon moved"*.
A member whose vendor set genuinely saw no change in the window is the one false positive; `staleDays`
is the knob, and the drift issue says so.

**When they fail** — a repo the census cannot classify is `unknown`, never uncovered, and a member the
freshness sweep cannot probe is `unknown`, never behind: no issue opened, no open issue closed on its
behalf, and a non-zero exit. A non-zero preprocessing subprocess fails the task, and the scheduler
converges one open `needs-human` issue for it.

**What the sweeps would like to align but cannot** — two repo *settings* decide whether a member's
baselining can deliver at all: *Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests* (without it
the maintenance PR is never created) and *Allow auto-merge*. Both are plain REST
(`PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/permissions/workflow`, `PATCH /repos/{o}/{r}`), so converging them here
alongside freshness would be the natural home — a sweep keeps them true, where adoption only sets them
once. It is not done because **`FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` is not an admin token**: both endpoints require
admin on the member, which this pack's PAT deliberately does not carry (its scope is Metadata +
Contents read, Issues read/write). So the settings stay an owner action, and the sweeps report the
*symptom* — a member stuck `behind` — rather than the cause. See #590.

# Future directions

Things the corpus **would** do but deliberately does not yet — each with the blocker that
stops it, so the next reader does not re-derive the idea and then re-discover the wall.

This file is **documentation, never prose**. Nothing here is injected into a session: a pack's
`prose: 'RULES.md'` is what loads at session start, and a deferred idea has no business
spending that budget. Entries move out of here when they are built (into the code and its
own docs) or when they are ruled out for good (deleted, with the reason in the commit).

Not a backlog — GitHub issues are the backlog, and every entry below names its issue. This is
the *reasoning*, kept where it survives the issue being closed, reopened, or renumbered.

---

## Fleet-wide repo settings the sheepdog sweeps cannot align

**Issue:** #590 · **Blocker:** credential scope

Two repository settings decide whether a member's baselining can deliver at all:

| setting | without it |
|---|---|
| *Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests* | the maintenance PR is never created (#585) |
| *Allow auto-merge* | an `auto-merge` member's PR opens and never lands |

Both are plain REST — `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/permissions/workflow` and
`PATCH /repos/{o}/{r}` — so converging them alongside the `fleet-freshness` sweep would be the
natural home: a sweep keeps them true, where adoption only sets them once and cannot notice a
later flip.

It is not done because **`FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` is not an admin token**. Both endpoints require
admin on the member, and this pack's PAT deliberately carries only Metadata + Contents read and
Issues read/write — widening it to admin-on-every-repo to fix a two-field settings drift is a
poor trade.

So the settings stay an owner action, and the sweeps report the *symptom* — a member stuck
`behind` — never the cause. Revisit if a narrower administration scope appears, or if the fleet
grows past the point where setting them by hand at adoption is reliable.

input.title: Plan: prove a canon change is safe for consumers — startup self-test, fixture rehearsal, live canary
input.body:
Implementation plan for #592. Answers the owner's question — *"how do you test baselining works when you're only working on Claudinite? Could you just force-trigger baselining on a random project and wait?"*

## The constraint that decides the design

`packs/basics/tasks/baselining/worker.mjs:470`:

```js
const CANON_URL = 'https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite.git';
git(['clone', '--depth', '1', CANON_URL, tmp]);
```

**Hardcoded URL, default branch, no ref parameter.** A live consumer can therefore only ever baseline against canon `main`.

So force-triggering a real project — which *is* already supported, `FORCE_TASKS` in `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES` on a `workflow_dispatch` run (#513/#516) — can only tell you a change was safe **after it has already merged and reached every other repo**. As a pre-merge gate it cannot work today.

That is the answer to "was that the direction": **the instinct is right, the mechanism needs one addition**, and it should not be the only layer.

---

## Phase 0 — make a canon branch rehearsable (prerequisite, small)

Add an optional canon ref to the worker: `CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF` (and `CLAUDINITE_CANON_URL` for a fork), defaulting to today's behaviour.

```js
const ref = process.env.CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF;
git(ref ? ['clone', '--depth', '1', '--branch', ref, url, tmp] : ['clone', '--depth', '1', url, tmp]);
```

Guard: when a ref is set, the run must **not** advance the stamp to that sha — a branch head is not on trunk, and stamping it is exactly the wedge this session hit by hand (`ref-not-on-trunk`; the #328 anti-rewind guard then refuses every later converge). Rehearsal runs deliver to a throwaway branch and never touch `.claudinite-checks.json`'s `ref`.

Without this, phase 3 can only run post-merge.

## Phase 1 — the startup self-test (highest value, smallest surface)

`engine/selftest.mjs` — mechanism-only, "can Claudinite run here?", explicitly not "does this repo pass its rules". Budget: well under a second, no network.

| assertion | the failure it would have caught |
|---|---|
| mount present, `.claudinite-checks.json` parses, stamp readable | #518 (mount stamp dropped → baselining self-skipped fleet-wide) |
| **every declared pack resolves and its manifest validates** | **#555 — would have fired on every consumer the same day, instead of surfacing 2 days later as a blocked converge** |
| declared local packs exist at their declared paths | half-migrated local pack |
| hooks in `.claude/settings.json` point at files that exist | #397 (`inject-pack-prose` importing a nonexistent module — active packs' prose silently never injected, fleet-wide) |
| mounted skills resolve, no dangling links | #424 (five dangling links reached `main`) |
| scheduler workflow present, cron parses | `no-scheduler` drift |
| migrations registry loads | a malformed record aborting every run |

**Runs at:** SessionStart (report-only — never block a session), end of bootstrap, and end of baselining preprocessing, where a failure is precisely the signal that should request the agent rather than reporting `ok`.

## Phase 2 — fixture rehearsal in canon CI (the pre-merge gate)

`packs-tests/rehearsal/` — synthetic consumer trees, one per shape:

- local pack with `worldRules` + `workRules` + bundled skills
- prose-only local pack
- no local pack
- chrome-extension shape (vendored release plumbing)
- a **dormant** member

For each, CI runs the *real* converge — `apply-vendor-set` → `converge-wiring` → `migrations/apply` — then the selftest and `check_the_world`, in **two modes**:

- **fresh** — fixture stamped at `HEAD~`: the ordinary nightly path
- **stale** — fixture pinned at an old stamp: forces migration *selection* to fire, so a record that is missing, misdated, or non-idempotent shows as a red canon PR

Runs on every canon PR, in seconds, hermetically. **This is the gate #555 needed.** Its weakness is honest: fixtures drift from what real repos look like, which is what phase 3 covers.

## Phase 3 — the live canary (the owner's approach, made safe)

A **dedicated canary repo**, not a real project. Adopting Claudinite for real, seeded to mirror the fixture shapes, and disposable — a rehearsal opens PRs and rewrites the mount, and doing that to EdFringeNow or gRatio means a failed rehearsal leaves a real project dirty.

Canon CI dispatches its scheduler with `FORCE_TASKS=basics/baselining` and `CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF=<PR branch>`, then polls the run. Green = a real repo really baselined against this branch.

- **on canon PRs touching `engine/`, `vendoring/`, `migrations/`, or any `pack.mjs`** — advisory at first, blocking once it has proven stable
- **on merge to canon `main`** — always, as the post-merge smoke test
- minutes, not seconds, which is why it does not replace phase 2

## Phase 4 — the rule, enforced over the diff

A check that fails a canon PR which changes:

- a **manifest field** (adds one, or makes one required)
- a **check's severity** or a rule's id
- a **vendored contract** (engine module signature, task field, stub shape)

…unless it also ships **either** a migration record **or** a rehearsal fixture exercising the change — and says which in the PR body. `consumer-safe-changes.md` states this principle today; nothing enforces it, which is why #555 merged green.

---

## Sequencing and cost

| phase | unlocks | rough size |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — selftest | catches the #555 class **on day one, everywhere**; useful alone | small |
| 0 — canon ref | prerequisite for pre-merge canary | very small |
| 2 — fixtures | the pre-merge gate; catches it **before merge** | medium |
| 3 — canary | proves it against a real repo | medium, mostly plumbing |
| 4 — the rule | stops the class recurring by omission | small |

**Recommended order: 1 → 2 → 0 → 3 → 4.** Phase 1 pays for itself immediately and independently; phase 2 is the actual gate. Phases 0+3 are the owner's approach and are worth doing, but they are the slow confirmation, not the fast gate — a rehearsal that takes minutes and needs a live repo cannot run on every canon PR, and a gate that does not run on every PR is not a gate.

Refs #592

## 1. TLDR — what's wrong and how to fix it

TLDR's three test workflows (`test-extension`, `test-server`, `test-requirements`) all trigger on `pull_request` **but every one is path-filtered**:

```yaml
paths: ['extension/**', 'shared/**', 'dev/build/**', ...]
```

A maintenance PR touches only `.claudinite/**`, `.claudinite-checks.json`, and `README.md` — **no filter matches**. So:

- `ciDispatchPlan` sees `pull_request` triggers → `hasPrCi = true` → the worker **arms auto-merge**
- no workflow's paths match → **zero checks ever appear**
- auto-merge waits for a green that cannot arrive → the PR sits open forever

It's the same end state as the no-CI repos, reached the opposite way: those had no CI to wait for, TLDR has CI that never runs.

**The fix I recommend: add a conformance workflow** — `pull_request` with *no* path filter, plus `workflow_dispatch`, running `check_the_world`. That's exactly what MissingBulbWebsite ("Claudinite world sweep") and ClaudiniteWebsite ("conformance") already have. It closes a second hole too: TLDR's 2 pre-existing `claudinite-isolation` blockers on `CLAUDE.md:4` and `dev/procedures/working-instructions.md:6` are invisible to CI *because of those same path filters*.

Two weaker alternatives: set `maintenance.delivery: "review"` (defers rather than fixes), or add `workflow_dispatch:` to the three test workflows (dispatch ignores path filters, so checks would appear — but it runs the full product suite for a mount-only change). Say the word and I'll add the conformance workflow.

## 2. #591 relocated

The note is out of `packs/sheepdog/RULES.md` and into a new **`docs/future-directions.md`** — deferred ideas, each with the blocker that stops it. `prose: 'RULES.md'` is injected into every session declaring the pack, so an idea nobody can act on shouldn't spend that budget. Deliberately **no link from any vendored pack file**: a pack reaching into the canon's `docs/` would dangle in every consumer — the `reference-integrity` class that reached `main` unnoticed in #424. PR #591 retitled and updated.

## 3. The plan — [#593](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/593)

**Your instinct was right, but it can't work as a gate today.** I checked: `worker.mjs:470` hardcodes `git clone --depth 1 CANON_URL` — default branch, no ref parameter. Force-triggering already exists (`FORCE_TASKS` via `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`), but a live consumer can only ever baseline against canon `main`. So force-triggering a random project tells you a change was safe **after it already merged and reached everything else**.

Five phases:

- **0** — add `CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF` so a consumer can baseline a canon *branch*. Prerequisite for your approach. Must not stamp the branch sha — that's the off-trunk wedge I hit by hand tonight.
- **1** — the **startup self-test** you proposed. Mechanism-only. The pack-manifest assertion would have caught #555 on day one on every consumer, and the hook-target assertion covers #397's class.
- **2** — **fixture rehearsal** in canon CI: real converge against synthetic consumers, run *fresh* and *stale* (the stale mode is what forces migration selection to fire — that's your "with and without a migration").
- **3** — the **live canary**: your approach, but pointed at a *dedicated disposable repo*, not a real project. A rehearsal opens PRs and rewrites the mount; a failed one shouldn't leave gRatio dirty.
- **4** — the **rule**, enforced over the diff, not just stated in `consumer-safe-changes.md`.

Recommended order **1 → 2 → 0 → 3 → 4**. The honest split: your canary is the stronger *signal*, the fixtures are the stronger *gate* — a rehearsal taking minutes and needing a live repo can't run on every canon PR, and a gate that doesn't run on every PR isn't a gate.

> ⚠️ **Open:** #591 (relocated, needs LGTM) · #593 (plan — wants your call on scope/order before I build) · TLDR conformance workflow (my recommendation above) · #590 · 40 orphan branches, UI-only.
>
> **Tonight is unaffected** by all of the above: all 13 repos carry the fixed worker with an on-trunk stamp and should baseline cleanly — TLDR excepted, which will arm and wait.

# The repo's check flow — the deterministic place the whole-repo Claudinite
# world sweep runs at each change. The site is static and has no test suite of
# its own yet; when it gains one, add it as a step ahead of the sweep rather

  workflow_dispatch:

input.title: Add an unfiltered Claudinite conformance workflow
input.body:
This repo's three test workflows are all path-filtered to the product tree (`extension/**`, `server/**`, `dev/requirements/**`), which is right for them and wrong for conformance: a PR touching only `.claudinite/**` matched **none** of them, so it started no check at all.

Two silent consequences:

1. **The nightly maintenance PR could never land.** `maintenance.delivery` is `auto-merge`, and GitHub's auto-merge is a queue for *checks* — the arm succeeded, no check ever ran, and the PR waited forever. Claudinite #588 fixed the *no-CI* case by merging directly; this repo is the other shape, where CI exists but cannot fire for a mount-only diff. It was the one repo that fix did not cover.
2. **Two blocking `claudinite-isolation` findings sat on `main` unnoticed** — on `CLAUDE.md:4` and `dev/procedures/working-instructions.md:6` — because nothing in CI had ever run the world sweep here.

## The workflow

`pull_request` with **no path filter**, plus `push: [main]` and `workflow_dispatch`.

The dispatch trigger is load-bearing, not decoration: a branch pushed and a PR opened by the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` emit no `pull_request` event (GitHub's recursion guard), so baselining starts this workflow explicitly on its maintenance branch. Without it the maintenance PR is back to having no checks.

## The two findings

Turning the sweep on surfaces them, so they're resolved here rather than left to fail the first run. Both are **orientation prose** — the routers naming where the vendored canon lives so a reader knows the guidance is injected rather than authored here — not code couplings. They take `accept` entries with reasons, the same pattern this repo already uses for the `barrier` rule on `server/README.md` and `extension/src/api.mjs`.

`check_the_world`: **0 blocking**, 40 advisory (all pre-existing `file-placement`).

## Upstream

Claudinite gains a `conformance-workflow` rule (advisory) that names this trap, so the next repo in this shape is told rather than silently stalling.

input.body:
`maintenance.delivery: auto-merge` arms GitHub's auto-merge, which is a **queue for checks**. Three CI shapes exist, and only one fails silently:

| shape | outcome |
|---|---|
| no `pull_request` workflow at all | baselining merges directly (#588) — coherent |
| an **unfiltered** conformance flow | the sweep runs, auto-merge lands on green — correct |
| a **path-filtered** flow | the arm succeeds and **no check ever runs** — the PR waits forever |

The third is invisible from every angle: the repo looks like it has CI, `hasPrCi` is true, the arm reports success, and the maintenance PR simply never lands. TLDR sat in it — all three of its test workflows filter to `extension/**`, `server/**`, `dev/requirements/**`, so a mount-only diff matched nothing. The same filters had also hidden two blocking `claudinite-isolation` findings on its `main` for as long as they'd existed (fixed in TLDR#156, which adds the workflow).

## The rule

`packs/basics/conformance-workflow.mjs` — a member should have a workflow running `check_the_world` on **every** pull request, unfiltered.

**Advisory, deliberately.** Shipping it blocking would turn every member lacking the workflow red on its very next baselining — which is exactly the #555 failure mode this rule exists to make less likely: a required thing added to the canon with no path for consumers to comply first. It becomes blocking once the fleet carries the workflow, and the promotion is a one-line change with the reasoning recorded in the file.

Relevance-first on the vendored mount, so it is inert in any non-member. A repo with **no** `pull_request` workflow is deliberately not flagged — that is #588's coherent shape, not a defect.

## Verification

Full CI test set **1029 pass / 0 fail**; `check_the_world` **0 blocking, 9 advisory** (all pre-existing `file-placement`). Ten see-it-fail cases, including the exact TLDR shape, and verified firing against the real TLDR tree before the fix and silent after it. `packs/README.md` corpus tally updated 66 → 67 in the same change, as its guard requires.

Refs #592

inject-preferences.sh
=== session-start-command.sh ===
#!/bin/bash
# SessionStart orchestrator — the ONE place the corpus-dependent session-start
# steps run, IN SEQUENCE, in a single process.
#
# Why this exists: Claude Code runs hook entries IN PARALLEL with
# non-deterministic order ("all matching hooks run in parallel… the order is
# non-deterministic" — the Claude Code hooks docs). So a populate-then-read
# chain spread across separate SessionStart entries is a race, not a sequence —
# the cause of intermittent "the harness didn't load this session" reports.
# Everything that reads the corpus therefore runs HERE, in order. The corpus is
# always already present: a consumer's tracked vendored mount, or the canon
# checkout itself.
#
# Each step's stdout is forwarded to this hook's stdout, which SessionStart adds
# to the session context (prose, preferences, halt-and-ask directives). Progress
# — a timestamp and what it is doing — is written to .claudinite-hooks.log and to
# stderr, so a triggering failure (no lines at all) reads differently from an
# execution failure (a step logged `start` but not `done`).
#
# Always exits 0: a SessionStart hook cannot block, and a non-zero exit makes
# Claude Code DISCARD this hook's stdout — including any step's halt-and-ask
# directive, the load-bearing safety gate. Failure is surfaced via the log and
# the injected directives, never the exit code.
set -uo pipefail
here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"  # <corpus>/engine/hooks
# This script lives in <corpus>/engine/hooks/. The preferences step lives
# beside it (per-user content is never vendored, so its step is hook machinery —
# see ../vendoring/DESIGN.md); the remaining step scripts live in the engine's
# loader dir (<corpus>/engine/pack_loader).
corpus="$(dirname "$(dirname "$here")")"

# --- durable hook log (format mirrored in engine/checks/helpers/hook-log.mjs —
# --- keep the two in step). Lives at the project
# --- root, OUTSIDE .claudinite/, beside the repo's own files. Best
# --- effort: logging must never fail a hook.
CLAUDINITE_LOG="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.claudinite-hooks.log"
CLAUDINITE_HOOK_RUN="${CLAUDINITE_HOOK_RUN:-$$}"; export CLAUDINITE_HOOK_RUN
# Bound the log across sessions (no-op when a Method B sync already trimmed it).
if [ -f "$CLAUDINITE_LOG" ] && [ "$(wc -c <"$CLAUDINITE_LOG" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -gt 262144 ]; then
  tail -n 400 "$CLAUDINITE_LOG" >"$CLAUDINITE_LOG.tmp" 2>/dev/null && mv "$CLAUDINITE_LOG.tmp" "$CLAUDINITE_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
hooklog() {
  local ts; ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"
  local line="$ts run=$CLAUDINITE_HOOK_RUN $1: $2"
  printf '%s\n' "$line" >>"$CLAUDINITE_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true
  printf '%s\n' "$line" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Run one step, forwarding its stdout to ours (→ session context) and logging
# its lifecycle. A step failing (they fail soft) never aborts the rest — hence
# no `set -e`. Tallies feed the one-line confirmation footer below.
ran=0; labels=""; warns=""
run_step() {
  local label="$1"; shift
  hooklog "$label" "start"
  "$@"
  local rc=$?
  hooklog "$label" "done exit=$rc"
  ran=$((ran + 1))
  labels="${labels:+$labels, }$label"
  [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && warns="${warns:+$warns; }$label exited $rc"
}

hooklog orchestrator "start"
run_step inject-preferences bash "$here/steps/inject-preferences.sh"
run_step load-active-prose  node "$corpus/engine/pack_loader/inject-pack-prose.mjs"
run_step mount-skills       node "$corpus/engine/pack_loader/mount-skills.mjs"
run_step env-check          node "$corpus/engine/pack_loader/env-requirements.mjs" check
# The interview machinery is the adoption skill's, bundled in the
# Claudinite-lifecycle pack — absent when the tree doesn't carry it, and then
# there is no interview.
interview="$corpus/packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/adopt-claudinite/interview.mjs"
[ -f "$interview" ] && run_step interview-check node "$interview" check
hooklog orchestrator "done"

# One terse, visible confirmation into the session context that the harness ran
# this session — the healthy-case counterpart to the loud halt directives. It
# reports that the machinery ran (not that every step succeeded semantically — a
# soft halt still exits 0), and flags any step that actually crashed.
end_ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"
summary="Claudinite session-start: ran $ran steps ($labels) at $end_ts."
[ -n "$warns" ] && summary="$summary WARNING: $warns."
printf '%s\n' "$summary"
exit 0

+  // 6b. SELF-TEST the converged tree before judging its content. This asks "can
+  //     Claudinite still run here?" — mount, stamp, pack manifests, hook targets,
+  //     mounted skills, cron, migrations registry — and it is the gate that would
+  //     have caught #555 the night it landed: a required manifest field arrived
+  //     with no migration, every consumer pack stopped validating, and because a
+  //     pack that fails validation contributes NO rules, check_the_world went on
+  //     reporting green about a corpus it was no longer running. A content check
+  //     cannot see its own machinery break. This runs on the just-converged tree,
+  //     so it judges what the member is about to live with.
+  const selftestOk = selfTestPasses(root);
+  if (!selftestOk) console.log('baselining: the converged mount FAILED its self-test — requesting the agent');
// 7. Escalation gate: run the conformance checks only when a change happened and
-  //    no agentic note already forces the agent.
+  //    no agentic note already forces the agent. A failed self-test forces it too:
+  //    broken machinery is exactly the judgment case, and merging it would spread

input.body:
Phase 1 of #593.

Deliberately **not** a conformance check. `check_the_world` judges the repo's *content* against the rules; this judges whether the *machinery* that would run those rules is intact. A repo can be perfectly conformant and still have a broken mount, a hook pointing at a deleted file, or a pack the loader silently drops — and none of that is visible to a content check, **because a rule that never runs reports nothing**.

## Why these probes

Every fleet-wide failure this corpus has had was that shape:

| probe | the failure it would have caught |
|---|---|
| `pack-manifests` | **#555** — a required manifest field with no migration; consumer packs stopped validating, and since a pack that fails validation contributes no rules, `check_the_world` kept reporting **green** about a corpus it was no longer running |
| `hook-targets` | **#397** — `inject-pack-prose` imported a module that didn't exist, so every active pack's `RULES.md` went un-injected fleet-wide for days |
| `stamp` | **#518** — `loadConfig` dropped the mount stamp, so baselining self-skipped everywhere and no run ever said so |
| `skill-links` | **#424** — five mounted skill links dangled on `main`, unnoticed |
| `mount`, `scheduler`, `migrations` | a half-vendored engine, an unparseable cron, a malformed record aborting every run |

None was caught by canon CI, because the canon's own tree is always already correct. All four would have fired on the **first session after the change, on the member, where the damage was**.

## Where it runs

- **SessionStart**, first and **report-only**. Never `--strict` there: a non-zero exit makes Claude Code discard the hook's stdout, which would throw away the very report it exists to deliver (and any halt directive with it).
- **Baselining preprocessing**, against the just-converged tree — and a failure now **escalates to the agent**. Broken machinery is the judgment case, and merging it would spread the breakage to a repo that was working an hour ago.
- Standalone `--strict` for bootstrap and CI.

## Design notes

- Pure probes over an injected `io`, so the whole set runs with no tree on disk.
- **Not-applicable is a distinct result from failure** throughout (`ok: null`) — the canon has no mount, a pre-cutover repo has no scheduler, a repo may mount no skills. Conflating those with failure is how a check earns a reputation for crying wolf.
- No probe reads another's result: a broken mount must not cascade into eight confusing failures.
- Never throws — a probe that cannot run is a failed probe with the reason attached, not a crash that takes the session-start orchestrator down with it.

## Verification

Full CI test set **1053 pass / 0 fail**; `check_the_world` 0 blocking. 21 unit tests, plus 3 covering the new escalation path.

**Mutation-tested rather than assumed**: neutering the stamp probe and neutering the hook-target probe each turn the suite red (20/1), so the tests bite. Also run live against the canon (5 probes pass) and two real consumers (6 probes pass), and the orchestrator's own test updated for the new step.

Refs #592, #593

## Preferences
