# Canary rules

This repo is the **live canary** for Claudinite's consumer-safety gate. It is not a product. It
carries no application code and it is meant to be disposable.

The canon's `canary-rehearsal.yml` workflow converges this repo against a candidate canon ref and
asks one question: *does a real member still work?* Everything here exists to make that question
answerable.

## Standing rules

- **Stay a realistic member.** The value of a canary is that it is real. Keep the vendored mount at
  `.claudinite/shared/`, the declaration, the hooks, the scheduler workflow, the conformance
  workflow, and this local pack. A stub proves nothing.
- **Keep the local pack loading.** `local/canary` is declared in `.claudinite-checks.json`. It must
  keep a valid `pack.mjs`, a rule in each scope, at least one bundled skill, and this file. That
  combination — manifest parse, two-scope dispatch, skill mounting — is the shape that broke the
  fleet in canon #555, and it is the shape this repo exists to cover.
- **The canary's own rules stay trivial.** They prove the pack loaded; they do not enforce anything
  about this repo. A rule with real opinions would turn the canary red for reasons unrelated to the
  canon ref under test, which destroys the only signal this repo produces.
- **Never hand-edit `.claudinite/shared/`.** It is vendored. Re-vendor from the canon instead —
  a hand-edit is silently reverted by the next converge and takes the rehearsal's meaning with it.
- **Divergence from `main` is expected and disposable.** A rehearsal may leave this repo converged
  against a candidate ref. Re-baselining it to canon `main` is always the right repair; there is no
  local state here worth preserving.

---
name: snapshot-approval
description: Get owner approval for a moved UI-snapshot baseline. Use whenever a change to a dev/requirements case (its spec or its rendering) makes the snapshot tests fail — the pixels moved and the baseline wants to change.
---

# Snapshot-approval process

The general principle — a moved snapshot/golden baseline needs owner approval,
not silent regeneration — is canon. This is the project process when a change
to a `dev/requirements/<kind>/cases/*` case makes the snapshot tests **fail**:

1. **Surface the diff immediately, don't carry on.** Revert the baseline to the
   committed **expected** PNG, run the snapshot test so it fails (the harness
   writes the rendered `actual` and a highlighted `diff` to
   `dev/requirements/shared/.artifacts/`), and send three images to the chat:
   **expected** (committed), **actual** (newly-rendered), and the **diff**.
   When the change alters the PNG's **dimensions** (e.g. a fixture shrink),
   pixelmatch can't diff unequal sizes so the harness writes only `actual` (no
   `diff`) — stitch **expected** and **actual** side-by-side into one image for
   the review instead.

=== ClaudiniteWebsite deploy-pages.yml ===
# Publishes site/ to GitHub Pages on every push to main that touches it.
# Artifact-flow deploy (no gh-pages branch); the custom domain (claudinite.com)
# is configured in the repository's Pages settings, not here — see
# site/README.md. Uploading site/ (never the repo root) keeps the agent-tooling
# dirs out of the artifact.
name: Deploy site to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: Inject Cloudflare Web Analytics token
        # The beacon token is public (it ships in the client), so it lives in a
        # repo *variable*, not a secret. When set, substitute it into the served
        # analytics.js; when unset, the placeholder stays and analytics no-ops.
        # sed uses '#' as its delimiter so the line contains no shell pipe.
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN" ]; then
            sed -i "s#REPLACE_WITH_CLOUDFLARE_WEB_ANALYTICS_TOKEN#${CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN}#" site/assets/analytics.js
            echo "Injected Cloudflare Web Analytics token from the CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN variable."
          else
            echo "CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN variable not set — analytics stays off (placeholder retained)."
          fi
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
        with:
          # First run enables Pages (source: GitHub Actions) if the token is
          # allowed to; otherwise enable it once in Settings → Pages.
          enablement: true
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: site
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

---
name: canary-role
description: What ClaudiniteCanary is for and how to work in it — the live canary for Claudinite's consumer-safety gate. Use before changing anything in this repo, and when a canary rehearsal comes back red and you have to decide what the red means.
---

# Working in the canary

This repo is Claudinite's **live canary**. Read this before changing anything here, because the
normal instinct — make the repo green, make the repo useful — is wrong in a specific way.

## The gate this repo is half of

Canon CI can prove a canon change is internally consistent. It cannot prove the change is safe for
**consumers**: the vendored mount, the pack loader, the hook wiring and the skill mounts only meet
a real repo on the other side of a vendor set. So the canon runs
`.github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml`, which converges *this* repo against a candidate canon ref
and runs the world sweep and the selftest against the result.

The gate's whole value rests on this repo being a **real, disposable member**. Real, or the
rehearsal tests a shape no consumer has. Disposable, or nobody will let the rehearsal converge it.

## What must not be removed

Anything that makes this a member is load-bearing:

- the vendored mount at `.claudinite/shared/` and the `.claudinite-checks.json` declaration
  that names what is vendored;
- the `.claude/settings.json` hook registrations;
- the vendored scheduler workflow, with the repo-hashed cron minute;
- the unfiltered conformance workflow — without it the maintenance PRs have no check to gate on,
  and with `maintenance.delivery: auto-merge` they queue forever behind a check that never runs;
- **the `local/canary` pack** — the highest-value shape here. Canon #555 broke the fleet through
  exactly this surface: a local pack's manifest, its rules in both scopes, its bundled skills.

## Reading a red rehearsal

A rehearsal failure is a claim about the **candidate canon ref**, not about this repo. Before
touching anything here, separate the two:

1. **Does the same failure reproduce against canon `main`?** If it does, the canary drifted or
   broke on its own and the candidate ref is exonerated. Re-baseline to `main` and re-run.
2. **Only the candidate ref fails?** That is the signal the gate exists to produce. Fix it in the
   canon. Do not fix it here — a canary patched to stay green is a canary that has stopped
   reporting.
3. **Never quiet a finding with an `accept` entry to get a rehearsal green.** An `accept` is a
   reasoned keep about *this repo's* content; using one to mask a canon regression converts a
   loud failure into a silent one, permanently.

## Repairing the canary

Re-baselining to canon `main` is always the correct repair, and there is no local state here worth
preserving. One caveat, from vendoring's anti-rewind guard (#328): the stamped `ref` in
`.claudinite-checks.json` must be an **ancestor of canon `main`**. Stamp a feature-branch sha and
the repo lands `ref-not-on-trunk`, which convergence then refuses to rewind past — wedging the
repo permanently. Rehearsals may stamp a candidate ref by design; a human repair should not.

# The Claudinite world sweep, on every pull request.
#
# Deliberately UNFILTERED — no `paths:` key. This repo is the canon's live
# canary: almost every change to it lands under `.claudinite/**`, which is
# exactly what a product-tree path filter would exclude. A filtered conformance
# workflow here would start no check at all on the changes that matter most.
#
# Two things depend on this workflow existing:
#
#   1. The maintenance PRs. `maintenance.delivery` is `auto-merge`, and GitHub's
#      auto-merge is a queue for CHECKS — with no check configured the arm
#      succeeds and the PR then waits forever. A canary whose nightly refresh
#      cannot land stops tracking the canon and stops being a canary.
#   2. The consumer-safety gate itself. The canon's canary-rehearsal converges
#      this repo against a candidate ref; the world sweep is the assertion that
#      answers whether a real member still works.
#
# `workflow_dispatch` is not decoration: a branch pushed and a PR opened by the
# Actions GITHUB_TOKEN emit no `pull_request` event (GitHub's recursion guard),
# so baselining starts this workflow explicitly on its maintenance branch.
# Without the dispatch trigger it cannot, and the PR is back to having no checks.
#
# The WORK scope is deliberately absent: it judges a session's own change against
# that session's transcript and runs at the Stop hook, not in CI.
name: Claudinite conformance

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  conformance:
    name: Claudinite world sweep
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # The engine's always-vendored Node CLI, invoked as the standalone command
      # — never as a test file a language runner discovers.
      - name: Claudinite world scope
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs

import pathlib, re

      # Every production release advances the version. package.json is the single
      # source of truth; the bumped file is committed back to main so the number
      # in the repo always names the last release that actually went out.
      - name: Bump version
        id: bump
        run: |
          NEW_VERSION=$(node scripts/bump-version.mjs)
          echo "version=$NEW_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Released version $NEW_VERSION"

      - name: Commit the version bump
        # [skip ci] keeps this commit from re-triggering this workflow, so there
        # is no deploy loop. Rebase-and-retry because the Claudinite scheduler and
        # its maintenance PRs also land on main, and a race here would otherwise
        # lose the bump and leave the repo claiming an older version than shipped.
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add package.json
          git commit -m "Bump version to ${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }} [skip ci]"
          for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
            if git push origin HEAD:main; then
              echo "Pushed the version bump on attempt $attempt."
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = "5" ]; then
              echo "Failed to push the version bump after $attempt attempts." >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Push rejected — rebasing on latest main and retrying (attempt $attempt)."
            git pull --rebase origin main
          done
'''

for repo, checkout in (("missingbulbwebsite", "actions/checkout@v4"), ("claudinitewebsite", "actions/checkout@v5")):

    # contents: write — the bump commit is pushed back to main
    t = t.replace("permissions:\n  contents: read", "permissions:\n  # write: the release commits its version bump back to main\n  contents: write", 1)

""", """  push:

input.body:
The site already deployed on every push to `main`, but nothing recorded **what** had been released — there was no version anywhere in the repo, so a deployed site and the repo that produced it could not be told apart.

## The change

Adopts the fleet's existing versioning idiom (the same scheme and script EdFringeNow uses):

- **`package.json`** — the single source of truth for the version. No dependencies, no build; the site is static and hand-authored. This file exists to hold the number.
- **`scripts/bump-version.mjs`** — `1.<mmdd>.<prev+1>`, so the patch advances monotonically even when the day rolls over and the minor changes.
- **`deploy-pages.yml`** — bumps, captures the version, commits it back to `main`, then deploys.

## Two details worth reviewing

**`[skip ci]` on the bump commit.** Without it the pushed bump re-triggers this workflow and the deploy loops forever.

**Rebase-and-retry on the push.** The Claudinite scheduler and its maintenance PRs also land on `main`. A plain push would lose the race silently and leave the repo claiming an older version than it actually shipped.

`permissions.contents` goes `read` → `write`, which the push back to `main` requires.

## Verified

The bump script run twice in sequence: `1.0.0` → `1.0731.1` → `1.0731.2` — the patch advances as intended. `check_the_world` is clean (0 findings). The seed is left at `1.0.0`, so the first real deploy produces `1.<mmdd>.1`.

A root `package.json` does **not** activate the `node` pack — activation is by declaration, and EdFringeNow has carried an undeclared one for months.

input.title: Release on every push to main, with a version bump
input.body:
Nothing in this repo recorded **what** had been released — there was no version anywhere, so a deployed site and the repo that produced it could not be told apart.

## The change

Adopts the fleet's existing versioning idiom (the same scheme and script EdFringeNow uses):

- **`package.json`** — the single source of truth for the version. No dependencies, no build; the site is static and hand-authored. This file exists to hold the number.
- **`scripts/bump-version.mjs`** — `1.<mmdd>.<prev+1>`, so the patch advances monotonically even when the day rolls over and the minor changes.
- **`deploy-pages.yml`** — bumps, captures the version, commits it back to `main`, then deploys.

## A judgement call to check

The trigger **loses its `paths:` filter**. It was `site/**` + the workflow file; it is now every push to `main`, matching MissingBulbWebsite so the two sites behave identically and every state of `main` is a released state.

The cost is honest: a `.claudinite/**`-only change — a nightly maintenance merge, say — now bumps the version and redeploys identical content. If you would rather the version tracked only site changes, restoring the `paths:` filter is a two-line revert and I'll do it.

## Two details worth reviewing

## Sites — [MissingBulbWebsite#31](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/pull/31) · [ClaudiniteWebsite#45](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/pull/45)

Neither site had a version *anywhere* — a deployed site and the repo that produced it couldn't be told apart. Both now adopt the fleet's existing idiom rather than a new one: EdFringeNow's `1.<mmdd>.<prev+1>` scheme and bump script, `package.json` as the single source of truth, bumped by the deploy and committed back to `main`.

Two things I want your eye on:

- **ClaudiniteWebsite loses its `paths:` filter** so both sites behave identically and every state of `main` is a released state. Honest cost: a nightly maintenance merge now bumps the version and redeploys identical content. Two-line revert if you'd rather the version tracked only site changes.
- **Rebase-and-retry on the bump push** — the Claudinite scheduler also lands on `main`, and a plain push would lose that race silently, leaving the repo claiming an older version than it shipped.

Verified by running the bump twice: `1.0.0 → 1.0731.1 → 1.0731.2`. Seed left at `1.0.0` so the first real deploy produces `1.<mmdd>.1`. Both sites stay conformant. And I checked the thing that would have bitten: a root `package.json` does *not* activate the `node` pack — activation is by declaration, and EdFringeNow has carried an undeclared one for months.

## Canary

`ClaudiniteCanary` is attached and cloned (README only). The subagent is bootstrapping it with a deliberately representative shape — a local pack with `worldRules`, `workRules` and a bundled skill, i.e. the exact #555 shape — plus an unfiltered conformance workflow, and must prove `check_the_world` 0 blocking and a passing self-test before it reports done.

One thing only you can do: once its PR merges, set the repository variable **`CLAUDINITE_CANARY_REPO`** on the canon to `missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary`. Until then `canary-rehearsal.yml` no-ops with a warning by design.

content.content:
# Claudinite per-repo task scheduler — the repo's ONLY cron
# (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §3). A thin shim: all logic lives in the
# vendored engine, so this file changes rarely (schema and behavior changes ride
# the vendor refresh, not edits here). It runs hourly on a repo-hashed minute
# constrained to :10–:50 — spreading the fleet, dodging GitHub's :00 stampede,
# and staying clear of the hour boundary the slot math anchors on.
#
# The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap/vendoring rewrites it to this
# repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`
# (scheduler-workflow-shape enforces the range; baselining re-derives the value to
# catch drift). `workflow_dispatch` allows a manual run; the concurrency group
# serializes runs so a slow run and its successor never overlap.
#
# A manual run may carry `overrides` — ONE free-form `KEY=value` string, because
# GitHub cannot declare arbitrary named inputs. It reaches the engine as
# `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`, and the engine understands exactly one key:
# `FORCE_TASKS=<comma-separated task ids>`.
# It runs those tasks even though their slot has already passed, and
# WITHOUT consulting their preconditions — forcing is the operator's decision, so
# nothing asks the task whether it agrees. The engine learns "run these ids",
# never what any of them do, and no task declaration mentions forcing at all.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '12 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      overrides:
        description: 'Manual-run overrides: comma-separated KEY=value. FORCE_TASKS=<task ids> runs those tasks unconditionally, even when their slot has passed, e.g. FORCE_TASKS=baselining.'
        required: false
        default: ''

concurrency:
  group: claudinite-scheduler
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; baselining's deliver() pushes the maintenance branch (agent-preprocessing §7/E4)
  issues: write          # file / label / close dispatch issues
  pull-requests: write   # baselining's deliver() opens the per-cycle maintenance PR and arms auto-merge
  actions: write         # read the run ledger (last successful run) for due-slot math, AND
                         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (store-release fires the release
                         # orchestrator's daily leg) — creating a workflow_dispatch event needs
                         # write, not read, and `read` silently 403s the POST

jobs:
  schedule:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Evaluate schedule and dispatch due tasks
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # Empty on every scheduled run — `inputs` is only populated by
          # workflow_dispatch. The engine reads only FORCE_TASKS out of it.
          CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES: ${{ inputs.overrides }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/run.mjs

  # A scheduled run reaches no one when it goes red, so escalate a whole-run
  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue (DESIGN §3.6,
  # gha/scheduled-failure-escalation). Converges to ONE open issue by a fixed
  # title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a first-run
  # failure may precede the scheduler's own label-ensure.
  report-failure:
    needs: schedule
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite scheduler run failed';
            await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' }).catch(() => {});
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${owner}/${repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const body = `The Claudinite scheduler run failed: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels: ['workflow-failure'], body });

input.body:
Adopts Claudinite into this repo, per `bootstrap.md`, at canon `main` **a76c355**.

## Why this repo is not a stub

ClaudiniteCanary is the **live canary** for Claudinite's consumer-safety gate. Canon CI can prove a canon change is internally consistent; it cannot prove the change is safe for **consumers** — the vendored mount, the pack loader, the hook wiring and the skill mounts only meet a real repo on the far side of a vendor set. The canon's `canary-rehearsal.yml` converges this repo against a candidate ref and asks whether a real member still works.

That question is only worth asking if this repo *is* a real member. So this PR adopts the full member shape, not a placeholder.

## What was adopted

| Piece | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Vendored mount | `.claudinite/shared/`, 146 files, via `apply-vendor-set.mjs` |
| Declaration | `.claudinite-checks.json` — packs, `taskScheduler`, `maintenance.delivery: auto-merge`, `badges.readme: auto` |
| Stamp | `{ "updated": "2026-07-31T19:07:38.876Z", "ref": "a76c355fe771c058f5d725995cf51337f597a2c8" }` |
| Packs | `basics`, `barriers` (via `basics`), `git-github` (via `basics`), `grow_with_claudinite`, `tidy-repo`, **`local/canary`** |
| Hooks | `.claude/settings.json` — SessionStart orchestrator, Stop, PreToolUse[Bash], SessionEnd |
| Ignore contract | the two hook-log lines, and nothing else |
| Scheduler | vendored `claudinite-scheduler.yml` on cron minute **:12** — the repo's hashed minute from `hash-minute.mjs missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary`, not a guess |
| Badges | README pack-badge row between the `claudinite:packs` markers |

The stamped ref is canon `main`, deliberately. A stamp that is not an ancestor of trunk leaves the repo `ref-not-on-trunk`, which vendoring's #328 anti-rewind guard then refuses to converge over — wedging the repo permanently. Verified: `git merge-base --is-ancestor a76c355 origin/main` passes.

Wiring was written by `converge-wiring.mjs`, which now re-reports `already converged` — so the nightly will not fight it.

## The canary-specific pieces

### A local pack — `.claudinite/local/packs/canary/`

This is the point of the exercise. Canon **#555** broke the fleet through exactly this surface: a manifest the loader must parse, rules in both scopes the runners must dispatch, bundled skills the mounter must link. A canon change that silently stops loading local packs has to fail *here*, loudly, before it reaches a member that carries real rules.

- `pack.mjs` — `id`, `ruleRoutingGuidance { belongs, excludes }` (both under the 20-word cap), `prose: 'RULES.md'`, `skills: ['canary-role']`
- `mount-present.mjs` — one `worldRule`: the vendored mount carries the engine
- `pack-intact.mjs` — one `workRule`: a change touching the pack leaves its manifest and prose in place
- `skills/canary-role/SKILL.md` — the bundled skill
- `RULES.md` — the pack's prose

**Both rules are deliberately trivial and deliberately non-firing.** Their job is to prove the pack *loaded*, not to enforce anything about this repo. A rule with real opinions would turn the canary red for reasons that have nothing to do with the ref under test — destroying the only signal this repo exists to produce. Each rule module is dependency-free (plain finding objects, no imports out of `.claudinite/shared/`), so the `claudinite-isolation` barrier holds.

### An unfiltered conformance workflow

`.github/workflows/claudinite-conformance.yml` — `pull_request` (no `paths:` filter), `push: [main]`, `workflow_dispatch` — running `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`.

Unfiltered on purpose: nearly every change here lands under `.claudinite/**`, which any product-tree path filter would exclude. Two things depend on it existing:

1. **The maintenance PRs.** `maintenance.delivery` is `auto-merge`, and GitHub auto-merge is a queue for *checks* — with none configured the arm succeeds and the PR waits forever. A canary whose nightly refresh cannot land stops tracking the canon and stops being a canary.
2. **The gate itself.** The world sweep is the assertion that answers whether a real member still works.

`workflow_dispatch` is load-bearing too: a branch pushed and a PR opened by the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` emits no `pull_request` event, so baselining must start this workflow explicitly.

### Documentation of the role

The README now says what the repo is for, and the `canary-role` skill covers how to read a red rehearsal: **it is a claim about the candidate canon ref, not about this repo.** Reproduce against canon `main` first; if only the candidate fails, fix it in the canon. Never quiet a finding with an `accept` to get a rehearsal green — that converts a loud failure into a silent one, permanently.

## Verification

All run locally against the working tree, exactly as pasted:

```
$ node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
$ echo $?
0
```

No output — `report-findings.mjs` prints the `N blocking, M advisory` summary only when there is at least one finding, so an empty run is **0 blocking, 0 advisory**.

```
$ node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs
$ echo $?
0

$ CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=/workspace/claudinitecanary node engine/selftest.mjs --strict
Claudinite self-test: 7 probes passed.
$ echo $?
0
```

The seventh probe is `skill-links`, which is `N/A` until the mounts exist; running `mount-skills.mjs` first makes it run and pass (6 passed + 1 skipped without it).

Because "green" and "actually wired" are different claims, two positive checks that the #555 surfaces are live rather than merely present:

```
$ node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list | grep canary
canary/mount-present  blocking  the vendored Claudinite mount is present at .claudinite/shared/  ...
canary/pack-intact    blocking  a change touching the canary pack leaves its manifest and prose in place  ...
```

(24 rules dispatched in total.)

```
$ node .claudinite/shared/engine/pack_loader/mount-skills.mjs
$ readlink .claude/skills/canary-role
../../.claudinite/local/packs/canary/skills/canary-role
```

The mount directory self-ignores, so nothing session-generated is committed.

The sweep also earned its keep during this change: a first draft of the README linked paths under `.claudinite/`, and `claudinite-isolation` raised 3 blocking findings on it. Fixed by rewording rather than by an `accept` — this repo is the last place that rule should be waived.

1	# The LIVE CANARY (#593 phase 3) — the required final step of any core change.
2	#
3	# The fixture rehearsal (packs-tests/rehearsal/) is the fast gate: hermetic,
4	# seconds, on every PR. It has one honest weakness — a fixture only tests what
5	# someone remembered to model. This is the other half: a REAL repo, really
6	# adopting Claudinite, really running its own scheduler, converged against this
7	# canon ref and asked whether it still works.
8	#
9	# WHY IT IS A SEPARATE WORKFLOW. It takes minutes, needs a cross-repo token, and
10	# mutates another repository's working tree. A gate with those properties cannot
11	# run on every push without becoming something people route around. So: manual
12	# dispatch, plus automatic on merge to main — the post-merge smoke test, which
13	# the owner's own framing settles as "still much much better than not knowing".
14	#
15	# WHERE THE CANARY IS NAMED. In `.claudinite-checks.json`, on the `local/claudinite`
16	# pack entry's `config.canaryRepo` — the same tracked pack-entry config mechanism
17	# the sheepdog pack uses for its fleet scope. NOT a GitHub repository variable: the
18	# binding between this canon and its canary is a fact about the project, and a
19	# repository variable is invisible in the tree, absent from every diff, and cannot
20	# be reviewed alongside the workflow that acts on it. A reader of this repo should
21	# be able to see which repo CI is about to rewrite.
22	#
23	# WHY A DEDICATED REPO, NOT A REAL PROJECT. A rehearsal rewrites the mount and
24	# can leave a failed converge behind. Pointing that at EdFringeNow means a bad
25	# canon commit leaves a real project dirty at the exact moment attention is
26	# elsewhere. The canary is disposable by construction; that is its whole value.
27	#
28	# WHAT PROTECTS THE CANARY ITSELF: the worker's rehearsal mode
29	# (CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF) converges, reports, and then RESTORES the working tree —
30	# no commit, no branch, no PR, and above all no stamp. Stamping a branch head
31	# would leave the canary `ref-not-on-trunk`, which vendoring's #328 anti-rewind
32	# guard then refuses to converge over: a rehearsal that wedges its own canary.
33	name: Canary rehearsal
34	
35	on:
36	  workflow_dispatch:
37	    inputs:
38	      ref:
39	        description: "Canon ref to rehearse (blank = this workflow's own ref)"
40	        required: false
41	        type: string
42	  push:
43	    branches: [main]
44	    # Only the surfaces a consumer actually vendors. A README or a doc change
45	    # cannot break a member, and spending minutes proving that teaches everyone
46	    # to ignore the result.
47	    paths:
48	      - 'engine/**'
49	      - 'packs/**'
50	      - 'vendoring/**'
51	      - 'migrations/**'
52	
53	permissions:
54	  contents: read
55	
56	concurrency:
57	  # One canary at a time: two rehearsals converging the same repo would race on
58	  # its working tree and report each other's damage.
59	  group: canary-rehearsal
60	  cancel-in-progress: false
61	
62	jobs:
63	  rehearse:
64	    name: Rehearse against the canary repo
65	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
66	    timeout-minutes: 20
67	    steps:
68	      - name: Check out the canon (for the declaration)
69	        uses: actions/checkout@v5
70	
71	      - name: Resolve the canary repo from the declaration
72	        id: cfg
73	        run: |
74	          CANARY=$(node -e '
75	            const c = require("./.claudinite-checks.json");
76	            const e = (c.packs || []).find((p) => p && p.id === "local/claudinite");
77	            process.stdout.write(e?.config?.canaryRepo ?? "");
78	          ')
79	          if [ -z "$CANARY" ]; then
80	            echo "::warning::No canary declared — skipping the live canary."
81	            echo "Add config.canaryRepo to the local/claudinite pack entry in"
82	            echo ".claudinite-checks.json, naming a disposable repo that has adopted"
83	            echo "Claudinite. Until then the fixture rehearsal is the only consumer gate."
84	            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
85	          else
86	            echo "Canary: $CANARY (from .claudinite-checks.json)"
87	            echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
88	            echo "repo=$CANARY" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
89	          fi
90	
91	      - name: Check out the canary
92	        if: steps.cfg.outputs.skip == 'false'
93	        uses: actions/checkout@v5
94	        with:
95	          repository: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.repo }}
96	          token: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
97	          path: canary
98	
99	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
100	        if: steps.cfg.outputs.skip == 'false'
101	        with:
102	          node-version: '24'
103	
104	      # The canary runs ITS OWN vendored worker, not this checkout's — that is
105	      # the copy a member would run, and testing anything else would be testing
106	      # a code path no consumer ever executes. The worker then fetches THIS ref
107	      # and converges the canary against it.
108	      - name: Rehearse
109	        if: steps.cfg.outputs.skip == 'false'
110	        env:
111	          CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF: ${{ inputs.ref || github.ref_name }}
112	          CLAUDINITE_REPO_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/canary
113	          CLAUDINITE_REPO: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.repo }}
114	          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
115	        working-directory: canary/.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/tasks/baselining
116	        run: node worker.mjs
117	
118	      - name: What a failure means
119	        if: failure()
120	        run: |
121	          echo "::error::The canary repo could not be converged against this canon ref."
122	          echo "A real consumer, on its real mount, either failed the self-test or went"
123	          echo "red on its own conformance sweep. This is the failure mode the fixture"
124	          echo "rehearsal is designed to catch early and the fleet is designed never to"
125	          echo "see: do not merge (or, post-merge, revert) until the canary is green."

**The gap:** canon CI proves the canon is healthy, which is not evidence about consumers — the canon's own packs are always already migrated, so a change that breaks every member passes it green. #555 did exactly that.

## The commits

| # | commit | phase |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `engine: a startup self-test — can Claudinite run here?` | 1 |
| 2 | `baselining: rehearsal mode — converge against a canon branch, stamp nothing` | 0 |
| 3 | `packs-tests: the baselining rehearsal — the gate #555 needed` | 2 |
| 4 | `claudinite: enforce the consumer-safe-change rule over the canon's own diff` | 4 |
| 5 | `canary: a live rehearsal against a real repo, and the procedure doc` | 3 |

### 1 — the self-test (`engine/selftest.mjs`)

Seven probes asking *can Claudinite run here?*, not *is this repo conformant*. Each traces to a real fleet-wide failure: `pack-manifests` (#555), `hook-targets` (#397), `stamp` (#518), `skill-links` (#424). Runs at SessionStart (report-only — `--strict` there would make Claude Code discard the hook's stdout) and in baselining preprocessing, where a failure now escalates to the agent. **Mutation-tested**: neutering the stamp probe and the hook-target probe each turn the suite red.

### 2 — rehearsal mode (`CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF`)

Lets a run converge against a canon **branch**. A rehearsal stamps **nothing** — a branch head is not on trunk, and stamping it leaves the member `ref-not-on-trunk`, which the #328 anti-rewind guard then refuses to converge over. Not hypothetical: that happened by hand to all thirteen members on 2026-07-30.

### 3 — the fixture rehearsal (`packs-tests/rehearsal/`)

Four fixture consumers × two modes, converged with the **real** scripts, then self-test and sweep. `stale` mode pins the stamp in the past so migration *selection* actually fires — that is the "with a migration" half.

**Verified by reproducing #555 faithfully** — schema gains a required field *and the same commit updates every canon pack*, as actually happened:

```
canon CI       0 blocking   ← green, exactly as it was on 2026-07-29
the rehearsal  FAILS        ← naming the consumer pack that no longer validates
```

A first draft of this passed while testing nothing: the sweep inherited the canon's cwd and reported on the canon. Fixed — each fixture runs as its own git repo with itself as cwd.

### 4 — `consumer-safe-change`

A work-scoped check over the canon's own diff. Touching the manifest vocabulary, a blocking rule's severity, or the scheduler stub requires **either** a migration record **or** a rehearsal fixture. Deliberately narrow: a rule that cried wolf on every commit gets turned off, and is then worth nothing on the day it matters.

### 5 — the canary + the procedure

`.github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml` converges a **dedicated disposable repo** against a canon ref — manual dispatch plus automatic on merge to `main`. It runs the *canary's own vendored worker*, since that is the copy a member runs. Inert with a warning until `CLAUDINITE_CANARY_REPO` names a repo.

`consumer-safe-changes.md` gains the three-layer procedure.

## Verification

**1079 tests pass, 0 blocking**, both scopes clean. (Late in the session this environment's signing helper exhausted its file descriptors, which fails any test that commits — including nine pre-existing `github-actions` fixtures. Unrelated to this change, but it exposed a real fragility, so commit 5 also makes the rehearsal fixtures independent of the host's signing config. The final commit is unsigned for the same reason.)

## Needs you

The canary repo does not exist yet — create a disposable repo, adopt Claudinite in it, and set the repository variable `CLAUDINITE_CANARY_REPO`. Until then phase 3 is inert and the fixture rehearsal is the only consumer gate.

- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/).
